title: VMC 86 550 sugarcane (NSIC Sc 11): Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: VMC 86 550 sugarcane: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: VMC 86 550 sugarcane is a sugarcane variety. See its days to harvest, yield, pest ratings, traits and where it grows best.
excerpt: VMC 86 550 is a registered sugarcane variety, also sold or known as NSIC Sc 11. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council (NSIC) in 2002 as NSIC 2002 Sc 11. Vict. Expt. Station bred it. It takes about 10.5 months from planting to harvest, with 162 LKg of sugar per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: If you came here looking for NSIC Sc 11, this is the same sugarcane. The facts below come from the NSIC registry kept by the Bureau of Plant Industry, with notes from its seller and farm sources. Compare it with the others in our [sugarcane variety finder](/crop-varieties/sugarcane), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for sugarcane](/land-preparation/sugarcane-land-preparation).

**Yield:** 162 LKg of sugar per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.caption: From the NSIC registry and its seller

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

VMC 86 550 sugarcane takes about 10.5 months from planting to harvest. That is about the average of the 16 sugarcane varieties with a day count, 10.8 months. Count the months from planting, and plan the harvest for a dry stretch when you can.

Its average yield of 162 LKg/ha matches the average of its group, 160.71. Sugar yield is counted in LKg, bags of 50 kilograms of raw sugar per hectare. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?

blocks.caption: Reactions in the registry trials, rated under natural field conditions

blocks.text: It was weak against downy mildew, smut, so scout for them from the early weeks. Read up on [Corn downy mildew](/diseases/corn-downy-mildew), [Rice field rats](/pests/rice-field-rats).

The pests and diseases that hit sugarcane fields most often: [Rice field rats](/pests/rice-field-rats), [Corn downy mildew](/diseases/corn-downy-mildew), [white grub](/pests/white-grub). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
Its stalks grew about 226 cm long and 2.7 cm thick. The fiber content is 13 to 14 percent. Trash: highly self trashing, which decides how much cleaning the cane needs before milling.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Harvest:** Matures in 10 to 11 months, best cut October to January.
**Fruit:** Stalks about 226 cm, 2.7 cm thick, fiber 13 to 14 percent.
Moderately susceptible to downy mildew and smut, resistant to leaf scorch, yellow spot and rust.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: a standard VMC cane, used as a parent of the PHILSURIN variety PSR 00 161. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant VMC 86 550 sugarcane

Mills pay for sugar, not cane, so compare the sugar yield in LKg per hectare as well as the tonnes of cane. Pick a variety that ratoons well, and one rated against smut and downy mildew, the diseases that cut a ratoon crop short. Before planting, get the field ready with our guide: [Land preparation in the Philippines](/land-preparation/land-preparation-philippines).

items: Buy sealed packs or tagged sacks from an accredited dealer, and check the packing date and germination rate.
Ask your municipal agriculturist or nearby farmers how it did in your area last season.
Try it on a small area first, beside the variety you usually plant, before you switch the whole farm.
Write down the planting day, inputs and harvest, so you can compare varieties on your own ground. anee.io keeps these records for you.

items.q: Is NSIC Sc 11 the same as VMC 86 550?
items.a: Yes. NSIC Sc 11 is another name for VMC 86 550, registered as NSIC 2002 Sc 11. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.

items.q: How long does it take to harvest?
items.a: It takes about 10.5 months from planting to harvest. Then the weather and your care decide the exact day.
The record shows 162 LKg of sugar per hectare on average in the trials. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of VMC 86 550?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
